tooltip: State School Fund: the main source of state money for K-12 school districts
definition: The primary source of state funding for Oregon's K-12 school districts. Districts use it to pay educator salaries, buy textbooks and maintain schools. The Legislature sets the amount for each two-year budget.

tooltip: Current service level: what it costs to keep existing programs going for the next two years
definition: The amount estimated to be needed to continue currently approved programs and services for the next two-year budget, using standard inflation assumptions. Budget writers start from it. For schools, the Department of Administrative Services calculates the State School Fund CSL; for 2027-29 it is $12.56 billion.

tooltip: Quality Education Model: the state's estimate of what Oregon schools need to meet the quality goals in law
definition: The state's own estimate of what it costs for Oregon's schools to meet the quality goals set in law. The Quality Education Commission updates it and publishes a report every two years, in August of even-numbered years. It prices two levels: the status quo (today's services) and the full QEM (what's needed to meet the goals). See "status quo QEM" and "full QEM" below.

tooltip: Quality Education Commission: the state commission that produces the Quality Education Model
definition: The commission the Legislature created in statute in 2001 to define the cost of meeting Oregon's quality goals for schools. It updates and publishes the Quality Education Model.

full_name: Joint Committee on Public Education Appropriation
tooltip: Joint Committee on Public Education Appropriation: reports whether the Legislature's school funding is sufficient
definition: The legislative committee that reports whether the state's school funding is sufficient to meet the quality goals in law. If it isn't, the report must say by how much and what that means for schools. By law it relies on the Quality Education Commission's findings.

tooltip: Education Stability Fund: a state reserve whose withdrawals must go to public education
definition: One of Oregon's two general reserve accounts; the other is the Rainy Day Fund. Created in 2002, it receives 18% of Lottery net earnings. Withdrawals need a three-fifths vote in each chamber plus either an economic trigger or a governor's emergency declaration, and must be used for public education.

tooltip: Office of Economic Analysis: the state's economic and revenue forecasters
definition: The state's economists, part of the Department of Administrative Services, who publish the Oregon Economic and Revenue Forecast. The forecast tells budget writers how much money the state expects to have. In this archive OEA always means this office; the teachers' union (Oregon Education Association) is written out in full.

tooltip: Department of Administrative Services: state agency that houses the revenue forecasters and calculates the State School Fund CSL
definition: A state agency. It houses the Office of Economic Analysis and calculates the State School Fund current service level used in the Quality Education Model report.

tooltip: Legislative Fiscal Office: the Legislature's budget office
definition: The Legislature's budget office. Its staff prepare budget documents for the Joint Committee on Ways and Means and publish Budget Highlights summarizing each adopted budget.

tooltip: Legislative Revenue Office: the Legislature's revenue office
definition: The Legislature's revenue office. After each session, the Office of Economic Analysis builds LRO's estimates of how new laws change revenue into the state forecast. LRO also publishes summaries of the state's reserve funds.

tooltip: Oregon Department of Revenue
definition: The state agency that publishes A Brief History of Oregon Property Taxation, the source this archive uses for Measures 5 and 50. It also assesses some property, such as public utilities and large industrial plants.

tooltip: Oregon Department of Education: the state's K-12 education agency
definition: The state agency for K-12 education. It supports the Quality Education Commission's work and carries out orders such as the Governor's instructional-time executive order.

tooltip: Student Success Act: 2019 law adding about $2 billion per two-year budget for education
definition: A 2019 law, funded by the Corporate Activities Act passed the same year, expected to invest over $2 billion in Oregon education every two years. About $700 million of that goes into the State School Fund (the "SSA transfer"); the rest goes to three other accounts.

tooltip: Public Employees Retirement System: the state pension system school districts pay into
definition: The retirement system that school districts and education service districts pay into for their employees' pensions. The PERS Board approves employer contribution rates in the fall of even-numbered years.

tooltip: Individualized Education Program: a plan of services for a student with a disability
definition: A plan that promises a student with a disability specific educational services, under the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act. Meeting those needs generally costs more than for other students.

tooltip: Executive order issued by the Governor
definition: An order issued by the Governor. For example, EO 26-06 (2026) directs ODE to preserve student instructional time.

tooltip: Senate Bill
definition: A bill introduced in the Oregon Senate, followed by its number (e.g. SB 141).

tooltip: House Bill
definition: A bill introduced in the Oregon House, followed by its number (e.g. HB 2767 of 2023).

tooltip: Oregon Legislative Information System: the Legislature's site for bills and committee documents
definition: The Legislature's online system where bills and committee meeting documents are posted. Many documents in this archive come from it.

tooltip: Oregon School Boards Association
definition: A statewide association of school boards. It is an advocacy group; figures it publishes are its own estimates.

tooltip: Coalition of Oregon School Administrators
definition: A statewide association of school administrators. It is an advocacy group; figures it publishes are its own estimates.

tooltip: Portland Public Schools
definition: The school district in Portland. Its own documents are kept in a separate PPS research archive.

A two-year budget period. Oregon budgets two years at a time, from July 1 of an odd-numbered year to June 30 two years later; 2027-29 is the next one. The state constitution requires the Legislature to fund schools sufficiently "in each biennium".

full_name: Status Quo Core K-12 State Funding
definition: The Quality Education Model's estimate of what it costs to maintain the current activities of Oregon's K-12 schools: $13.78 billion in state funding for 2027-29. It counts funding sources beyond the State School Fund, so it is higher than the SSF current service level. This site calls it "keep today's services".

The Quality Education Model's estimate of what it costs to keep current services and add the investments needed to improve student outcomes: $16.21 billion in state funding for 2027-29. This site calls it "meet the state's goals".

The difference between what the Quality Education Model says is needed and what the state funds. The constitution requires the Legislature to report the extent of any such shortfall and its impact on meeting the quality goals.
Oregon's other general reserve account besides the Education Stability Fund, created in 2007. Unlike the ESF, its withdrawals don't have to go to education.
Oregon's law that returns income tax surpluses to taxpayers when actual collections beat the forecast by 2% or more over a two-year budget. It makes it harder for the state to build up reserves.

The Governor's proposed two-year state budget. By law it goes to legislators no later than December 1 of each even-numbered year (Dec 1, 2026 for 2027-29). The Legislature then writes the final budget.

full_name: Joint Committee on Ways and Means
definition: The Legislature's joint budget committee. Its Education Subcommittee writes the State School Fund budget bill (for 2025-27, SB 5516).
A 1990 ballot measure that introduced limits on property tax rates. Fully in effect by 1995-96, it cut tax rates an average of 51% from 1990-91 levels.
A 1997 ballot measure that cut property taxes, limited growth in assessed value and replaced most tax levies with permanent tax rates.
